cells.note: The study text supports the direction of the accountability moderation; the exact subgroup effect sizes and k values are reported in the wiki entry.

O.outcome_detail: time and effort required to determine errors

cells.quote: The handiness of this little apparatus may enlarge the usefulness of the test. It has already been suggested that the test is capable of being employed as a test of quickness in learning. If so used this form of apparatus will reduce the amount of work and the time required for performing the test very considerably.
cells.note: The study describes a proposed reduction in work and time but reports no comparative data or statistical test for the apparatus.

O.outcome_detail: performance on individual Scientific Method Test problems

cells.quote: Those problems which show a constant increase, from grade to grade, in the per cents of pupils solving them, are the best for the purpose. Those which behave erratically have to be regarded with suspicion. Obviously, if the sixth grade scores lower upon a given problem than the fifth, that problem does not measure progress from fifth to sixth grade ability.
cells.note: The study reports a methodological item-selection criterion rather than a quantified treatment effect; erratically behaving problems were eliminated in earlier editions, and no effect size is printed.

cells.quote: From six to twelve per cent, more work is accomplished in the first minute of a ten minute test in the fundamentals of arithmetic, than is accomplished in the average of the later minutes of the test.
cells.note: The study does not report random assignment or counterbalancing.

result.effect: Addition: 0.80 vs 0.81; subtraction: 1.11 vs 1.26; multiplication: 5.32 vs 5.49; division: 2.80 vs 2.34

cells.quote: The average amount of error in the first minute in addition was .80, in the remaining minutes it was .81. In subtraction it was 1.11 and 1.26 respectively. In multiplication it was 5.32 and 5.49, and in division 2.80 and 2.34.
cells.note: Lower error is treated as better performance; division is the exception, with more errors in the first minute.

result.effect: Coefficient of variability 8% to 17% lower in the first minute

cells.quote: The coefficients of variability, i. e., the ratios of the average deviations to the medians are from 8 per cent, to 17 per cent, lower in the first minute than in the later minutes.
cells.note: The study also reports that average deviations were generally 0% to 2% lower in the first minute.

result.effect: Girls about 4% more work and about 4% fewer mistakes

cells.quote: The girls' entire accomplishment is about 4 per cent, in excess of the boys. A tabulation of the errors by sexes shows that the boys made about 4 per cent, more mistakes than the girls.
cells.note: Sex groups were observed rather than randomly assigned; the study reports that boys did better in the eighth grade.

D.treatment: 400–700 ms ERP component during retrieval practice

O.outcome_detail: ERP component predicted current retrieval success

cells.quote: Liu et al.54 revealed that an ERP component occurring between 400 and 700 ms after the presentation of retrieval cues predicted both current and subsequent retrieval success, potentially reﬂecting the elaboration and strengthening that occur during retrieval attemp ts.
cells.note: The Perspective reports an association, but does not state its direction or provide an effect size.

O.outcome_detail: Later ERP component associated solely with subsequent retention

cells.quote: Furthermore, a later component between 700 and 1000 ms was associated solely with subsequent retention, serving as a neural marker for re-enco ding after a successful retrieval.
